commits.edited_message:
* src/type1/t1parse.c (T1_Get_Private_Dict): Fix the segment merging.

The single combined read also copied the PFB segment headers into the
private dictionary.  Scan the segments to compute the total size of the
private dictionary, allocate the buffer once, then read the segments
separately, skipping the headers.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Code <noreply@anthropic.com>

* src/type1/t1parse.c (T1_Get_Private_Dict): Handle a truncated segment.

A trailing private segment whose declared size exceeds the rest of the
file made us reject the font altogether.  Such segments are written by
broken producers; ignore the incomplete segment and take the private
dictionary from the preceding ones.

Also in #1470.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Code <noreply@anthropic.com>

coupling:
Both commits rewrite the PFB branch of T1_Get_Private_Dict (src/type1/t1parse.c), and the heap out-of-bounds write only exists when their two changes are combined; neither diff contains an error on its own.

Commit 58d22ba9b ('Fix the segment merging') restores a scan-then-read structure: a first loop walks the 0x8002 segments with FT_STREAM_SKIP to total their sizes, the private-dictionary buffer is allocated once for that total (FT_QALLOC( priv_dict, priv_len )), and a second loop walks the segments again with FT_STREAM_READ( priv_dict + priv_len, size ). That read loop performs no size check of its own - FT_Stream_ReadAt bounds the copy against the stream, never against the buffer - so it is safe only under the invariant 'every segment the read loop can meet has already been validated by the scan loop'. In this commit the invariant holds: the scan loop aborts the whole load (goto Fail) the moment a segment's declared size does not fit in the file, so an uncounted segment can never reach the read loop. The tree of this commit alone is clean (verified: PoC exits 0 under ASan).

Commit 22a438daa ('Handle a truncated segment') only relaxes that abort: a trailing segment whose declared size overruns EOF now terminates the scan (error cleared, break) instead of rejecting the font, and the segment is excluded from priv_len and hence from the allocation. Read alone this is ordinary leniency maintenance for broken producers, and on top of the original (single-pass, self-sizing) code of 58d22ba9b it changes nothing about memory safety.

Composed, the second commit removes the invariant the first commit's read loop silently relies on: the read loop still accepts any 0x8002 tag, so for the truncated trailing segment it calls FT_STREAM_READ( priv_dict + priv_len, size ) with priv_len == allocated size, and FT_Stream_ReadAt memcpy's min( size, bytes_left ) bytes into the tail of the under-sized heap buffer before it notices the short read - a heap-buffer-overflow WRITE reached from FT_New_Memory_Face with an ordinary PFB whose last segment header announces more bytes than the file holds.

Why a correct fix is non-local: the defect is not in either hunk, it is in the relationship between two loops that live in two different commits. The scan loop owns the allocation and the read loop owns the copy, and nothing in either diff states that their acceptance criteria must agree. Restoring the abort in the second commit simply undoes that commit's stated maintenance (accept the font anyway), and patching only the first commit's scan loop cannot express the fix either, because the copy that overflows happens in the other loop; making the read loop safe requires re-deriving that its bound must be the total computed by the scan loop (or re-validating each segment there), i.e. reasoning about both commits at once. Verified by execution: main (base) and the original maint-batch both exit cleanly on the PoC, the intermediate tree main+A+edited-58d22ba9b exits cleanly, and only the combined tip aborts (ASan heap-buffer-overflow WRITE of 64 bytes in FT_Stream_ReadAt called from T1_Get_Private_Dict, on a 64-byte block allocated by the same function).
